candidate_sentences.text: During the first three months of 2026, AS Amber Latvijas balzams experienced a significant deterioration in financial performance, driven by severe external challenges, geopolitical pressures, and disruptions within its affiliated corporate group.

In January 2026, the commencement of bankruptcy proceedings for related group company Stoli Group under Chapter 11 in the United States caused the Company to lose control over operations within that jurisdiction, directly impacting the solvency of its largest customer and its own capacity to meet creditor obligations.
Additional headwinds included adverse actions by Russian authorities against group entities following public support for Ukraine, alongside a broader downturn in the global spirits market.
These combined pressures severely strained cash flow and resulted in overdue excise tax liabilities, prompting the State Revenue Service to freeze the Company bank accounts.

verified_key_information_units.information: The company initiated Legal Protection Proceedings (LPP) in January 2026 (court-approved in February) to restructure liabilities and stabilize operations; the deadline for the LPP action plan was later extended to October 2026, with legal effects remaining in force until August 2026.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Filed LPP application on 30 January 2026, approved on 5 February 2026; court set initial plan deadline of 5 June 2026, later extended to 5 October 2026; legal consequences remain until 5 August 2026.

candidate_sentences.text: To ensure business continuity and protect creditors, the Company filed for legal protection proceedings, which were approved by the Riga City Court in February 2026 to facilitate liability restructuring and operational stabilization.

verified_key_information_units.information: The LPP filing automatically triggered an event of default under the Principal Shareholder's (Amber Beverage Group Holding S.à r.l.) bond documentation, which in turn triggered events of default under its bank financing arrangements.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: The filing of the LPP application also automatically triggered an event of default for Amber Beverage Group Holding S.à r.l. under the terms of its issued bond documentation. This, in turn, automatically triggered events of default by the Principal Shareholder under its financing arrangements with banks.

verified_key_information_units.information: Subsequent to the report period, in April 2026 the Principal Shareholder initiated judicial reorganization proceedings (réorganisation judiciaire) in Luxembourg, receiving a four-month moratorium until August 2026, during which enforcement actions against bondholders are suspended.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Pursuant to the judgment of the Luxembourg District Court sitting in commercial matters dated 24 April 2026, Amber Beverage Group Holding S.à r.l. has been authorized to initiate judicial reorganization proceedings; the Court has granted the Principal Shareholder a four-month moratorium until 24 August 2026, which suspends enforcement actions and collateral enforcement.

details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary demonstrates strong internal logical coherence. All statements build sequentially from external challenges (geopolitical pressures, bankruptcy of Stoli Group) to financial consequences (cash flow strain, account freezes) and finally to operational responses (legal protection proceedings, cost reductions). The financial metrics show consistent deterioration patterns (sales volume, turnover, gross profit, operating loss, net loss, EPS) with clear cause-effect relationships explained in adjacent sentences. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational breakdowns. While the summary covers multiple negative developments, the progression from causes to effects to responses forms a coherent narrative arc without redundancy or confusion.
